issues: whether a knife that opens via a flipper/thumb-stud mechanism activated by one-finger pressure, swinging fully open and locking, qualifies as a 'prohibited weapon' under the Criminal Code definition incorporated by tariff item 9898.00.00 (automatic/centrifugal/gravity knife)
whether the fact that similar knives are commercially sold elsewhere in Canada is relevant to classifying imported goods as prohibited weapons under the Customs Act
whether absence of domestic criminal charges for possession or sale of similar knives affects the customs classification or admissibility determination
whether intended personal or gift use rather than resale affects classification of goods as a prohibited weapon under tariff item 9898.00.00
what test applies to determine whether a knife opens by centrifugal force, gravity, or thrust versus by manual manipulation for purposes of the prohibited weapon definition
what is the correct procedure and standard of review for appealing a CBSA re-determination under the Customs Act to the Canadian International Trade Tribunal
key_facts: approximately ten inexpensive folding knives imported by mail from an overseas seller
each knife has a flipper/tab near the pivot allowing one-finger opening
pressing the flipper causes the blade to swing out rapidly and lock open, and cannot be slowed or stopped once started
CBSA detained the knives on entry and refused entry as prohibited weapons
client requested a re-determination and the original decision was confirmed
client intends to appeal to a trade tribunal
client argues similar knives are sold openly in Canadian retail stores
knives were purchased for personal/gift use, not resale
client states no criminal charges have been laid domestically for possession or sale of similar knives
causes_of_action: appeal of CBSA re-determination of prohibited-goods classification under the Customs Act
challenge to classification under tariff item 9898.00.00 (prohibited weapons)
search_terms: knife opens by centrifugal force test
